claims.claim: The Chief Justice attacked unemployed Indian youth in general
claims.claimed_by: public interpretations of 15 May reported oral remarks
claims.assessment: The reported language caused controversy; on 16 May the Chief Justice said his criticism was limited to people entering professions with false credentials. Full hearing recording and exact context remain unavailable.
claims.confidence: moderate in dispute; low for a definitive reading of intent

claims.claim: CJP was registered as an Indian electoral political party in August 2026
claims.claimed_by: Question raised by use of party name
claims.assessment: CJP publicly described itself as a pressure group rather than a party pursuing elections. An independently inspected contemporaneous ECI registration record is still needed for a definitive registry determination.
No transfer, donor, contract, verified filing or funding ledger establishing this allegation was obtained in this research session. Absence of a record is not a proof of no funding.

claims.claim: CJP alone caused Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
claims.assessment: Minister's resignation and broad multi-group protests are reported. An exclusive causal attribution to a single organisation is not established.
contradiction: Many student groups and actors had demands

claims.claim: Seven Goa protest detentions were judicially questioned
claims.assessment: The Indian Express quotes a High Court order questioning legal authorisation and reporting release. Original signed order is still outstanding; no final finding against individual police officers is established.

claims.claim: A 198-method resemblance means CJP was directed by Gene Sharp organisations
claims.claimed_by: hypothetical allegation for testing, not an identified CJP critic
claims.assessment: A published taxonomy of common protest techniques is not evidence of training, consultation or financing. Direct documents would be required.
contradiction: No verified direct relationship in reviewed material
claims.confidence: high about the inference rule, unassessable about all private contacts
